text:
lucy_sales: FYI incoming RFP from FinHealth LATAM. Core asks: Brazil + Germany only, BYO-HSM (on-prem HSM reachable from our nodes, mutual TLS), static egress IP per tenant, hard egress cap (<=20TB/month), and a 6-week pilot. They want an onboarding cost and steady-state monthly with a line-item breakdown. Also they request p99 API latency <120ms. Any infra or legal blockers?

dev_presales: Thanks. Need to validate we can meet p99 <120ms for their workload (mostly short chat calls, 512 token horizon). Also confirm HSM protocols supported (KMIP vs PKCS11). Are we OK with on-prem HSM calls from our regional nodes?

omar_infra: We have coloc partner in Se3o Paulo (partner-Z) and dedicated racks in eu-central-1. We can establish peering to customer's HSM endpoints. Important: some HSM vendors only allow outbound TLS from specific ports; we may need firewall rules.

rebecca_security: Security questions: 1) wire protocol (KMIP/PKCS#11) 2) client certs and mTLS requirements 3) do they require crypto material to ever be cached/held by us? If they insist on zero key exposure we must ensure all wrapping/unwrapping happens on their HSM and we store only references. Need their attestation and HSM vendor SOC/CC reports.

alex_ops: For static egress we can allocate a per-tenant NAT block. Example candidate NATs (subject to partner allocation):

```
EU-TENANT-NAT: 3.5.140.0/24
BR-TENANT-NAT: 34.202.160.0/27
```

Cost note: reserved egress IP blocks add $650/month per /24-equivalent block (prorated for smaller blocks). Also configuring strict regional-only egress (no cross-region fallback) requires a one-time network hardening project. Estimate lead time: 5 business days for BR partner routing, 3 days for EU.

dev_presales: What about the hard egress cap enforcement? Can we meter and throttle at 20TB and notify before throttling?

alex_ops: Yes, we can set hard caps per-tenant with alerts and soft-throttle rules. Enforcement options: email + webhook at 80/90% thresholds, then block at 100%. There's a SLA impact if we block traffic — we should surface as constraint to customer.

rebecca_security: If we block at 100% they'll experience outages; legal needs to sign off on limits and failure modes. Also if HSM calls fail due to network hardening we need an approved fallback plan.

nina_legal: We'll add a subprocessor addendum listing partner-Z and upstream cloud providers. For disabling cross-border fallback we require a routing exception addendum with risk acknowledgement and a modified liability cap. I can draft templates.

billing-bot: Quote helper: base pilot SKU = DED-PILOT-6W, reserved-IP-SKU = NAT-RESERVE, one-time-hardening = NET-HARDEN-1.

alex_ops: Rough numbers for budgeting (ballpark, partner costs TBD):

- Pilot (6 weeks): $18,000 (reserved 2x A100 slices, partner egress setup, reserved NAT blocks, monitoring)
- Ongoing minimal dedicated: $13,000/month + egress bandwidth fees
- Egress rates estimate: BR $0.11/GB, EU $0.035/GB (partner surcharge in BR)

Breakdown monthly: compute/reserved GPUs ~$9,000; network (egress reserve + NAT) ~$2,500; support/SLAs ~$1,500; if strict no-cross-region fallback add a one-time project fee $4,000.

lucy_sales: Can we provide a sample cost for the 20TB cap? Alex, quick calc?

alex_ops: 20TB = 20,480 GB. If split evenly BR/EU assumed 50/50: 10,240 GB * $0.11 = $1,126.4 for BR; 10,240 GB * $0.035 = $358.4 for EU. Total egress ~$1,485/mo. So monthly total ~ $14,485/mo. If BR is heavier it scales accordingly.

dev_presales: OK useful. We should also capture latency risk: partner-Z link from BR may have variable tails. Recommend offering a canary during pilot to validate p99 SLA; if they need contractual p99 we should add an SLA credit/penalty line.

nina_legal: SLA credits for p99 miss are doable but will affect pricing. I'll draft an SLA appendix for pilot+ongoing. Also need customer to sign HSM connectivity waiver and provide vendor security attestations.

omar_infra: Operational note: enabling strict regional-only routing will increase failover RTO from usually <5m to up to 60m in some edge cases because we can't use global fallback. We'll document in runbook.

deploy-bot: Created ticket D-20110 1 - finhealth-latam-byo-hsm: regions [sa-east-1, eu-central-1], nat-reserve=true, strict-routing=false (ops to confirm).

lucy_sales: Action items: Dev_presales to request HSM protocol + vendor reports; Alex to prepare 1-page quote with the line-item breakdown and 20TB example; Nina to prepare routing exception + SLA appendix templates; Omar to confirm lead times for partner-Z and exact NAT CIDRs. We'll reconvene once we have HSM details. :thumbsup:

dev_presales: On it, ping me if they push for cross-border key escrow options.

alex_ops: I'll include a variant quote that includes optional global fallback (with cost delta) and one without.

lucy_sales: Thanks team, I'll brief FinHealth tomorrow with the conservative numbers and the list of docs we need from them.
